What is the ArtVis Embedding Explorer?
• Interactive visual exploration of artists
in the ArtVis knowledge graph
• Combines artist embeddings with
graph-based views
• Supports exploration of artist groups,
similarities, differences, and
relationships
• Different views provide complementary
information
6

How to read the Embedding Map
• Each point represents one artist
• Artists positioned close to each other
have similar embedding
representations
• Colors represent computed clusters
• Artists without a cluster are shown as
unclustered / noise
• Distances should be interpreted
together with the additional graph
information
7

Computed clusters vs. ArtVis Groups
Computed clusters ArtVis Groups
• Automatically identified from the • Recorded artist groups in the
artist embeddings ArtVis knowledge graph
• Artists are grouped based on • Represent known group
patterns in the embedding space memberships in the dataset
A computed cluster is not the same as an ArtVis Group.

Free Exploration
Explore an artist, ArtVis Group, or art-historical question that
interests you.
● Follow whatever you find interesting
● Think aloud while exploring
● Record micro-entries when you notice relevant patterns
● You can change your direction at any time
● If you are unsure how to continue, I can provide a backup
exploration prompt
20

Think Aloud
During the exploration:
• Say what you are looking for
• Say what you notice
• Say what you are thinking or trying to understand
• Mention anything that is confusing or unexpected
There are no right or wrong answers.
21

Micro-Entries
When you notice an interesting pattern or observation, record a short micro-entry
For each entry:
● What pattern do you notice?
● How would you explain this pattern?
Additional notes:
● You can create multiple entries
● You can update an earlier entry if your explanation
changes
● Entries can be short

Interview Questions
● What did you explore or discover, if anything, and what helped you reach that
interpretation?
● Which views or interactions did you find useful, and which were confusing? Can
you give examples?
● How could the tool support your art-historical work? What would you still need to
check using other sources, such as literature or catalogues?
● Was there any information or functionality missing? What improvement would be
most important to you?
